newsitem.title: USA: Xerox names IBM's Richard Thoman president, COO.
newsitem.headline: Xerox names IBM's Richard Thoman president, COO.

text.p: Xerox Corp. on Thursday named Richard Thoman, the No. 2 executive at International Business Machines Corp., to the post of president and chief operating officer.
Thoman joined IBM in 1994 and was named chief financial officer in 1995. He is widely credited with turning around IBM's personal computer business.
In a statement, Xerox said Thoman will report directly to Xerox Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Allaire in a newly formed Office of the Chairman.

IBM said its senior vice president and chief counsel, Lawrence Ricciardi, would assume Thoman's responsibilities on an interim basis. He will continue to be responsible for IBM's legal, government and intellectual property functions.
News of Thoman's departure sent shares of IBM lower in pre-market activity. IBM was singled out for pre-open selling, falling to $86 a share from $87.25.

Thoman is the second chief financial officer to leave since Louis Gerstner became chairman of the giant computer maker. Jerome York, the previous chief financial officer, left IBM to work for billionaire Kirk Kerkorian.
"We are pleased that Rick Thoman is joining Xerox. He makes a strong management team stronger and provides a fresh perspective to help lead Xerox into the 21st century," Allaire said.

Allaire will focus on strategy and governance. Thoman will have day-to-day operating responsibilities for all Xerox document businesses worldwide, including marketing, sales, service and administration; and manufacturing, technology and product development.

"Xerox is an American icon -- a cherished part of this country's heritage," said Thoman. "Just as important, it is a prominent international company with outstanding growth prospects around the world. I am happy to join the family and proud to be able to help lead Xerox into the future."

Thoman, 52, has been with International Business Machines since 1994. He joined the company as group executive for the Personal Systems Group, which includes the IBM Personal Computer Company, and was promoted to chief financial officer in 1995.
Prior to joining IBM, Thoman was president and chief executive officer of Nabisco International.
